```{r setup}
library(lab6)

RNGversion(min(as.character(getRversion()), "3.5.3"))
set.seed(42)
n <- 2000
knapsack_objects <- data.frame(
  w = sample(1:4000, size = n, replace = TRUE),
  v = runif(n = n, 0, 10000)
)

```

## Introduction

The knapsack problem is where you choose a subset of items to maximize total value without exceeding a fixed weight capacity

## Brute force search

```{r}
brute_force_knapsack(knapsack_objects[1:12, ], W = 3500)
```

```{r}
system.time(brute_force_knapsack(knapsack_objects[1:16, ], W = 3500))
```

## Dynamic programming

```{r}
knapsack_dynamic(knapsack_objects[1:500, ], W = 3500)
```

```{r}
system.time(knapsack_dynamic(knapsack_objects[1:500, ], W = 3500))
```

## Greedy heuristic

```{r}
greedy_knapsack(knapsack_objects[1:800, ], W = 3500)
```

```{r}
set.seed(42)
n <- 1000000
big <- data.frame(w = sample(1:4000, n, replace = TRUE),
                  v = runif(n, 0, 10000))
system.time(greedy_knapsack(big, W = 3500))
```

## Profiling and optimization

```{r, eval = FALSE}
profvis::profvis({
  greedy_knapsack(big, W = 3500)
})
```

I compared the original and the optimized `greedy_knapsack` on 1,000,000
items with `bench::mark()`:

| Version   | Median time | Memory allocated | GCs |
|-----------|-------------|------------------|-----|
| Original  | 32.2 ms     | 36.4 MB          | 2   |
| Optimized | 26.3 ms     | 26.7 MB          | 1   |

The optimized version is about 1.2 times faster and allocates about 27%
less memory.
